status: DRAFT shaped plan by akiendell_cc_0, 2026-11-14, for akienasus to cast and chart. Not cast. Builds BEFORE b0c0c47835c1.
title: a gate firing's observation lands in a data_recorder, so something is there to inspect
intention: Every firing of a TransitionGate (build, entry, exit, emission) writes its structured observation (gate, timestamp, verdict, check counts, record, mismatches: the shape _collect_feedback already builds) into a DataRecorder at the holder's instance-space address, whether or not the gate's dial tree was ever constructed. The record is the same; only its home changes from a directory that production never creates to the recorder outline 17.7 names.
why: Measured 2026-11-14: TransitionGate._collect_feedback returns at once when self._tree is None, and nothing outside proofs calls construct(), so no gate has written a feedback record in production; akiendell has no feedback directory and the Dell, counted by the orchestrator, has records.jsonl only in codemother/0/tools/charter/inbound (302) and inferenceproxy/0/tools/data_recorder/metrics (18). The b0c0 probe, the data_recorder charter (17.7) and the gate charter's feedback route all expect gate observations in a recorder.
traces_to: Law 4 (a feedback loop nobody feeds is policy), Law 5 (the gate's story lives beside the holder), Law 1 (reuse the record shape _collect_feedback already built).

clauses.claim: after a green and a red firing of a gate whose tree was never constructed, the recorder holds two records, each with gate, verdict, checks_total, checks_passed and checks_failed, and the red one carries its mismatches

a firing never raises or slows the gate: if the recorder cannot be written, run() still returns or raises exactly what it did before (the feedback write is best-effort and loud in the log, never the gate's verdict)

decisions.text: D1: _collect_feedback writes through DataRecorder.write(record) at instance_path('codemother', 0)/tools/data_recorder/<gate name>/ (the holder is a CC call: the gates' calibration is build_inspector's, which moves into codemother in 93fa3e3a6199); the tree/feedback-directory branch is removed because nothing constructs a tree in production.

D2: the existing proof cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_gate_feedback.py changes with it: test_green_produces_feedback, test_red_produces_feedback, test_feedback_carries_sieve_data and test_no_feedback_without_construct read the recorder; the last one is replaced by a tooth that no construct() is needed. The two new teeth (clauses 1, 2) are added under this ticket's PROVES key.

measured.saw: MOST OF b0c0 IS ALREADY BUILT, so v1 and v2 of this plan (a new gate_inspection.py module) would have paralleled it (Law 1). cairn/tools/base/probes/gate_parameters_adjust_from_feedback.py already has _read_feedback, build_prompt, parse_proposals, inspect(records, resolver) which calls BUILD_GATE.adjust per proposal, a Threshold and an enough() predicate; cairn/tools/base/gate_class.py TransitionGate._collect_feedback already writes a structured record after EVERY gate firing (gate, timestamp, verdict, checks_total/passed/failed, record, mismatches); adjust() returns the prior state and cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_gate_feedback.py covers green/red feedback, adjust, revert and the refusals. What is missing is the WIRING, both measured: (1) _collect_feedback writes only when self._tree is set, and `.construct(` has no caller outside proofs (git grep), so BUILD_GATE._tree is None in production and no feedback is ever written: find ~/.cairn for a feedback dir returns none on akiendell, and the Dell has no gate recorder either (orchestrator 2026-11-14: records.jsonl only in codemother/0/tools/charter/inbound (302) and inferenceproxy/0/tools/data_recorder/metrics (18)); (2) the probe's _carry needs context['resolver'] and nothing in the repo injects one (it answers 'no resolver in context'). Note also that the probe reads BUILD_GATE._feedback_dir (files), not a data_recorder, though cairn/tools/data_recorder/intention+why.json says gate feedback lands there (17.7).
measured.how: read the probe, gate_class.py, test_gate_feedback.py; git grep '.construct(' and 'resolver'; find ~/.cairn for feedback dirs and records.jsonl; the orchestrator's Dell count

unmeasured: how many gate firings a day there are and so how fast a recorder grows (the data_recorder has clear(ids); no retention is decided here); whether writing per firing slows the commit path (the write is one JSONL append, not measured)
